A Starsim model is a sim (`ss.Sim`) that holds a population and a set of modules: one or more diseases, and whatever else the model needs (contacts, births and deaths, interventions). This page covers how those parts fit together, and how to check that the model Starsim built is the one you meant. For a first walk through a model, see [T1 – Getting started](../tutorials/t1_intro.qmd) and [T2 – Building a model](../tutorials/t2_model.qmd).

## A model and its parts

Here is a simplified measles outbreak in a town of 100,000 people: an SIR model, in which people are susceptible (S), infectious (I), or recovered and immune (R). Each susceptible person is infected at a rate of β = 1.9 per day times the fraction of people who are infectious, and people are infectious for 8 days on average:

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## Python

```{python}
import starsim as ss

S, I, R = ss.states('S I R')
infection = S >> I @ 1.9*I        # From S to I, at a rate of 1.9 per day times the fraction infectious
recovery  = I >> R @ ss.days(8)   # From I to R, after 8 days on average
measles = ss.Disease(infection, recovery, init_prev=0.001)

sim = ss.Sim(measles, total_pop=100_000, stop=ss.days(50))
sim.run()
sim.plot()
```

## R

```r
library(starsim)

states("S I R")
measles <- Disease(
  infection = Transition(S, I, rate = 1.9 * I), # From S to I, at a rate of 1.9 per day times the fraction infectious
  recovery  = Transition(I, R, dur = days(8)),  # From I to R, after 8 days on average
  init_prev = 0.001
)

sim <- Sim(measles, total_pop = 100000, stop = days(50))
sim$run()
sim$plot()
```

## Explicit

```{python}
S, I, R = ss.State(name='S'), ss.State(name='I'), ss.State(name='R')
infection = ss.Transition(source=S, dest=I, rate=ss.perday(1.9)*I, name='infection')       # From S to I, at a rate of 1.9 per day times the fraction infectious
recovery  = ss.Transition(source=I, dest=R, dur=ss.expon(mean=ss.days(8)), name='recovery') # From I to R, after an exponentially distributed time of 8 days on average
measles_explicit = ss.Disease(transitions=[infection, recovery], init_prev=0.001, name='measles')

sim_explicit = ss.Sim(
    diseases  = measles_explicit,
    networks  = ss.contacts(1), # Everyone mixes with everyone, with one contact per person per day
    total_pop = 100_000,
    start     = ss.days(0),
    stop      = ss.days(50),
    dt        = ss.days(1),     # Steps of a day
    unit      = 'day',          # The unit of bare numbers
    solver    = 'ode',          # Run as an ODE
)
sim_explicit.run()
sim_explicit.plot()
```
:::

The "Explicit" tab is the same model with nothing left for Starsim to fill in (the transitions in full, the exponential infectious period, homogeneous mixing with one contact a day, the unit, the step, and the solver), and gives the same results ([below](#checking-a-model)).

A sim can hold these kinds of modules, each given to it by keyword (a disease can also be given first, as here):

| Kind | What it is for | Keyword | See |
|---|---|---|---|
| Diseases | The states people can be in, and how they move between them | `diseases=` | [Diseases](building_diseases.qmd) |
| Networks and contacts | Who meets whom: contact matrices, mixing pools, and networks of individual contacts | `networks=` | [Places and data](populations_places.qmd), [Mixing](populations_mixing.qmd) |
| Demographics | Births, deaths, and pregnancy | `demographics=` | [Demographics](populations_people.qmd#births-and-deaths) |
| Interventions | Vaccination, testing, treatment, and changes to parameters | `interventions=` | [Products](interventions_products.qmd), [Interventions](interventions_interventions.qmd) |
| Connectors | Links between modules, such as one disease making another more likely | `connectors=` | [Connectors](interventions_connectors.qmd) |
| Analyzers | Extra results, collected as the sim runs | `analyzers=` | [Analyzers](interventions_analyzers.qmd) |

The sim itself holds what applies to the whole model: the population (`total_pop=`, or `n_agents=` for a model run as agents), the period (`start=`, `stop=`, and the time step `dt=`), and the random seed, and how the model is run (`solver=`). See [Running sims](running_sim.qmd) for these, and its [appendix of every sim setting](running_sim.qmd#appendix-every-sim-setting); see [Time](building_time.qmd) for the span and the step.

A disease can be **declared**, as states and transitions, as above, or **written as code**, for what states and transitions can't say; both kinds can be in the same sim. See [Diseases](building_diseases.qmd#diseases-as-classes), [Custom modules](building_modules.qmd), and [What can be declared](building_declared.qmd).

## Shorthand and its written-out form

This page is the reference for how a declared model is written; [Diseases](building_diseases.qmd) says what each kind of transition means. The operators are a short way to write `ss.Transition()`, and each form below builds the same objects as its written-out form, with the same results:

| Shorthand | Written out | Means |
|---|---|---|
| `S, I, R = ss.states('S I R')` | `S = ss.State(name='S')`, and so on | The states |
| `S >> I @ 1.9*I` | `ss.Transition(S, I, rate=1.9*I)` | A rate (a bare number after `@` is a rate) |
| `I >> R @ ss.days(8)` | `ss.Transition(I, R, dur=ss.days(8))` | A duration, or a distribution of durations |
| `I >> R @ dict(dur=ss.days(8), p=0.99)` | `ss.Transition(I, R, dur=ss.days(8), p=0.99)` | Any keywords of the transition |
| `I >> {ss.dead: 0.002, R: None} @ ss.days(8)` | `ss.Transition(I, {ss.dead: 0.002, R: None}, dur=ss.days(8))` | One transition with several destinations |
| `S + V >> I @ 1.9*I` | `ss.Transition([S, V], I, rate=1.9*I)` | From any of several states |
| `U >> A @ ss.on(ss.person.age >= 15)` | `ss.Transition(U, A, when=ss.on(ss.person.age >= 15))` | A trigger |
| `ss.Disease(infection, recovery)` | `ss.Disease(transitions=[infection, recovery])`, or `ss.Disease(infection=..., recovery=...)` | The disease, named after its variable |

A disease can also be a class, with the same lines in its body, or declare them in `__init__()` with `define_states()` and `define_transitions()` ([Diseases](building_diseases.qmd#diseases-as-classes)). Names and values that aren't given are filled in by the rules in the [appendix](#appendix-what-starsim-names-and-fills-in), and units by those in [Time](building_time.qmd#units).

## Checking a model

A short model leaves a lot unsaid, and Starsim fills it in. `describe()` lists the whole model as it was built: every state, transition, parameter, and setting, with each value that Starsim chose itself marked as **guessed**, and the rule it used.

```{python}
sim.describe()
```

Here three things were guessed: that the infectious period is exponential ([Durations](building_diseases.qmd#durations)), that everyone mixes with everyone, with one contact a day ([Stratification](building_stratification.qmd)), and that the model runs as an ODE ([Solvers and backends](running_solvers.qmd)). The [appendix](#appendix-what-starsim-names-and-fills-in) lists every guess. A guess is not an error, just a choice you didn't make, and it goes away when the value is given. Here the infectious period and the solver are given, so the only guess left is the mixing:

```{python}
S, I, R = ss.states('S I R')
infection = S >> I @ 1.9*I
recovery  = I >> R @ ss.erlang(k=4, mean=ss.days(8)) # Less spread than an exponential
measles = ss.Disease(infection, recovery, init_prev=0.001)

sim = ss.Sim(measles, total_pop=100_000, stop=ss.days(50), solver='ode')
sim.describe()
```

### Equations, diagram, and transitions

`equations()` writes out the differential equations of a declared disease, with its parameters by name (here `beta` and `dur_I`, the mean time in I). They hold whatever the model is run as: as agents, each person moves between states at the same rates.

```{python}
S, I, R = ss.states('S I R')
infection = S >> I @ 1.9*I
recovery  = I >> R @ ss.days(8)
measles = ss.Disease(infection, recovery, init_prev=0.001)

measles.equations()
```

`diagram()` draws the model's diagram, with each arrow labeled with its transition's name and value:

```{python}
measles.diagram()
```

A dashed arrow is a transmission, and a solid one any other transition; a transition with `p=` also gives the fraction that takes it. `measles.diagram('text')` gives it as a [Mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org) flowchart instead, for GitHub, wikis, and anything else that draws Mermaid. For every disease of a sim, and how they act on each other, use `sim.diagram()` and `sim.equations()`.

`transitions` is a table of the transitions, with what drives each (a rate or a duration) and its kind: a transition is a **transmission** if people catch it from people in another state (here, "transmission, from I"), and **spontaneous** otherwise. Printing it also shows which state leads to which:

```{python}
measles.transitions
```

### The reproduction number

`R0()` works out the basic reproduction number from the next-generation matrix of the model. For a simple SIR model this is β × the infectious period (1.9 × 8 ≈ 15), but `R0()` works for any declared model, including those with several infectious states, groups with their own contacts, or vectors:

```{python}
measles.R0()
```

`R0()` on a disease on its own assumes homogeneous mixing. For a disease in a sim with contacts or groups, use the sim's copy of it, `sim.diseases.measles.R0()`, which includes them (see below for why the sim has a copy).

::: {.callout-note}
The sim prints R0 when it starts. If some people start immune (e.g. `init=dict(I=0.001, R=0.9)`), it also gives the reproduction number in the population as it starts (often called the effective reproduction number, R): "R0 = 15.2 (R = 1.51 at the start, with 10% susceptible)".
:::

After a run, `Rt()` gives the reproduction number at each time point, from the people in each state and the rates as they were then (so it drops while an `ss.modify()` lowers β). It works for a run of any solver:

```{python}
sim = ss.Sim(measles, total_pop=100_000, stop=ss.days(50), verbose=0).run()
sim.diseases.measles.Rt().plot()
```

## Where the parts of a sim go

A sim runs a copy of each module it is given, so that the same disease can go into several sims (for example, one for each scenario) without one run changing another. After a sim is initialized (by `sim.init()`, or by `sim.run()`, which initializes it if needed), its copy of each module is in `sim.diseases`, `sim.networks`, and so on, by name. A disease made with `ss.Disease()` is named after its variable (here `measles`), and one made from a class after the class (`sir`); `name=` gives it a name of its own (see the [appendix](#appendix-what-starsim-names-and-fills-in)).

```{python}
sim = ss.Sim(measles, total_pop=100_000, stop=ss.days(50), verbose=0)
sim.run()

print(sim.diseases.measles is measles) # The sim's copy, not the original
print(sim.diseases.measles.pars)        # The disease's parameters
print(sim.results.measles.keys())       # Its results
```

- The parameters of each module are in `sim.diseases.measles.pars` (and `sim.pars.measles`); see [Parameters](building_parameters.qmd).
- The results are in `sim.results`, by module: `sim.results.measles.I`. Every state and every transition has a result of the same name. See [Outcomes](building_outcomes.qmd) for declaring more, and [Results](building_results.qmd) for working with them.
- In a model run as agents, the people are in `sim.people`, with each person's age, sex, and the states of each disease; see [People and demographics](populations_people.qmd). Each module adds its states to the people, so `sim.people.to_df()` gives a table with a row for each agent and a column for each of their attributes and states:

```{python}
sim = ss.Sim(measles, n_agents=1000, total_pop=100_000, stop=ss.days(50), dt=ss.days(0.25), verbose=0) # A quarter-day step, short enough for measles as agents
sim.run()
sim.people.to_df().head()
```

In a compartmental run, `sim.people` has a row for each group instead.

## Checks and pitfalls

A model that runs is not necessarily the model you meant, and a plausible plot is not enough to show that it is. These checks catch most mistakes in a new model:

- **Read `describe()` once for each new model**, and give any value it guessed that matters to your question.
- **Check that everyone has a place to start.** `init_prev` starts people in `E`, not `I`, in an SEIR model ([Starting values](building_diseases.qmd#starting-values-births-and-deaths)).
- **Check that the states add up.** In a closed model (no births or deaths), the people in all the states of a disease add up to the population at every time point.
- **Match the quantity to the question.** New infections are a flow (`res.infection`), and the number infectious a stock (`res.I`): summing `I` over time counts each person once for every day they are infectious.
- **Check the units of β.** Adding a contact matrix or a network changes β from a rate per person to a rate per contact; see [Mixing](populations_mixing.qmd).
- **Don't change the original after the sim is made.** Since the sim has a copy, changing `measles` after `ss.Sim(measles, ...)` has no effect on that sim. Change the sim's copy, give the new value to the sim by name (`ss.Sim(measles, pars=dict(beta=1.5))`), or make a new sim.

## Further reading

- [EpiModel](https://www.epimodel.org/): building and checking compartmental and network models in R
- [odin](https://mrc-ide.github.io/odin/): writing compartmental models as equations in R, compiled to C
- [epydemix](https://epydemix.readthedocs.io/): compartmental models with transitions declared by name, in Python
- [SimInf: an R package for data-driven stochastic disease spread simulations](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/SimInf/vignettes/SimInf.pdf): models declared as compartments and transitions, run as continuous-time Markov chains
- [Compartmental models in epidemiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compartmental_models_in_epidemiology): the SIR family, with their equations and R0

## Appendix: what Starsim names and fills in

From some names and forms, Starsim works out what the model didn't say. Each value it chooses itself is marked as guessed in `describe()`, with the rule it used; giving the value removes the guess.

**Settings:**

| What | What Starsim does | To say otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| The population | 10,000 people | `total_pop=`, or `n_agents=` as agents |
| The length of the run | 50 units of time | `stop=` or `dur=` |
| The unit of time | From the diseases' typed values, then dates, a typed `dt`, years, or the other modules' typed values; else time is in steps ([Time](building_time.qmd#units)) | `unit=`, or type every value |
| The solver | An ODE, or agents if anything in the model needs them ([Solvers](running_solvers.qmd)) | `solver=`, or `n_agents=` |
| Mixing | Homogeneous, one contact per unit of time | `networks=` |
| A single duration (`ss.days(8)`) | Exponential, with that mean | A distribution, e.g. `ss.erlang(k=4, mean=ss.days(8))` |
| A non-Erlang duration run as compartments | As many Erlang stages as match its mean and standard deviation | `stages=` on the transition |
| How the epidemic starts | A disease with transmission and no starting values starts with 1% of people infected, in the states a transmission (or else an acquisition) leads to: `E` in an SEIR | `init_prev=`, `init=`, or `init_n=` |
| Where people start, and births with no state go | The state named `S` or `susceptible` (in any case), else the one state transmission infects people from, else the first state made; and the only state with no starting value, if the first has one | `default_state=` on the disease, or `init=` |
| The fraction of the last branch | 1 minus the others, when one `p=` is `None` or left out | `p=` on every branch |
| A parameter given only bounds | The middle of its bounds | A value |
| The fractions and kind of a dimension | From the population, the world's ages, or equal fractions; age for ages, a place for a geography, else plain groups ([Stratification](building_stratification.qmd#levels-and-fractions)) | Fractions, and `kind=`, on `stratify()` |
| Aging | People age only if anyone is born or dies | `aging=True` or `False` |
| A named population's ages | The year the sim starts | `ss.population('Kenya', year=...)` |
| Results by group | Every step, or every few steps if every step would take more than about 100 MB | `results=` on the sim |

**Names:**

| Name or form | What Starsim does | To say otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| A variable that holds a state, transition, parameter, result, or disease made with `ss.Disease()` | Names it after the variable (`measles` is `sim.diseases.measles`, or `sim.measles`). A variable whose name starts with `_`, or is named like a setting of the sim, doesn't | A keyword, or `name=` |
| A transition with no name | `infection` for the disease's only transmission, else `<source>_to_<destination>` (`I_to_R`) | A variable, a keyword, or `name=` |
| A disease made from a class (`ss.SIR()`) | Named after its class, in lower case (`sir`) | `name=` |
| A disease held in no variable, or transitions given straight to the sim | Named from the first letters of its states (`sir`, `seir`); two with the same name are an error | `name=` |
| A delivery, product, or modifier | Named after its variable, or numbered (`screen`, `screen_1`) | `name=` |
| A module given as a string | `diseases='sis'`, `networks='random'`, or `dict(type='sir', ...)` is the class of that name, in lower case | Give the module itself |
| A path | `'flu.I'`, `'flu.pars.beta'`, or `ss.ref('hpv18.X')` is a part of a module by name, e.g. in `who=` or `ss.modify()` | |
| A result by its short name | `sim.results.I` is `I` if only one module has it | `sim.results.flu.I` |
| The names every module has (`step`, `sim`, `pars`, `name`, `results`, and its other methods) | An error as the name of a state, transition, parameter, or result | Another name |
| The keywords `init`, `init_n`, `init_prev`, `default_state`, `pars`, `strains`, `stratify`, `solver`, `name`, `label`, and `dt` | Settings of the disease; any other keyword with a plain value sets the parameter of that name, and is an error if there is none | |
| The arguments `self`, `sim`, and `uids` of a function | Given by name: the module, the sim, and the people a value is for | |

**Parameters.** A number written in a declared disease becomes a parameter, named by where it is, so that it can be given by name (`pars=dict(...)`) and fitted:

| Where the number is | Its name |
|---|---|
| Multiplying a source of infection (`1.9*I`) | `beta`, or `beta_<transition>` if the disease has more than one transmission |
| A duration, the only way out of its state | `dur_<state>` (e.g. `dur_I`) |
| A duration of a transition out of a state with several ways out | `dur_<transition>` (e.g. `dur_death`) |
| Any other rate (`ss.perday(0.001)`, `ss.prob(0.01, 'week')`) | `rate_<transition>` |
| The fraction of a separate transition, `p=` | `p_<transition>` |
| `init_prev=` | `init_prev` |
| Anything else: a factor such as the 0.5 in `0.5*A`, the fractions of one transition's destinations, starting values, an outcome's fraction or delay | Not a parameter; wrap it in `ss.par()` to make it one |

```{python}
S, E, I, A, R = ss.states('S E I A R')
example = ss.Disease(
    infection = S >> E @ 0.5*(I + 0.5*A),                    # beta (the 0.5 on A is not a parameter)
    onset     = ss.Transition(E, {I: 0.6, A: 0.4}, dur=ss.days(5)), # dur_E (the fractions are not parameters)
    recovery  = ss.Transition(I, R, dur=ss.days(7), p=0.99), # dur_recovery and p_recovery, since I has two ways out
    death     = ss.Transition(I, ss.dead, dur=ss.days(9), p=0.01),
    clear     = A >> R @ ss.days(5),                         # dur_A
    waning    = R >> S @ ss.prob(0.01, 'week'),              # rate_waning
    init_prev = 0.001,
)
example.pars
```

**Parts of the model:**

| Name or form | What Starsim does | To say otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| A bare state in a rate (`I` in `beta*I`) | Makes the transition a transmission by contact, and the state infectious. A rate on a count (`1.9e-5*I.n`) is a transmission too, but not by contact, so a network doesn't carry it | Write the rate you mean |
| An acquisition | Every transmission, or else each transition out of the first state; what `rel_sus`, a product's efficacy against acquisition, and `ss.treat` act on | `acquisition=` on the transition |
| The infected states | Those people are infected into and those that infect them; none, if nothing is transmitted. They give the results `infected` and `prevalence`, and are what a test detects and a treatment cures | `infected = E + I + H` on the disease, `ss.State(infected=True)`, or `ss.states(..., infected='E I H')` |
| A result or state called `infected` or `prevalence` | Kept, in place of the one Starsim would add (with a state `infected`, no `prevalence` is added) | |
| Every state and transition | A result of its own name: a stock for a state, a flow for a transition (with `.cum`), and `<transition>.<state>` for each destination of a split | |
| An expression given to the disease (`prevalence = I/N`) | A result, named after its variable or keyword; in a class body, one whose name starts with `_` is a helper, not a result | |
| `ss.unborn`, `ss.dead`, `ss.outside`, `ss.stay` | Outside the model: where births come from, where deaths go, and where people arrive from or leave to alive; `ss.stay`, as one destination of a split, keeps people where they are | |
| `ss.birth()` and `ss.death()` with no state | A birth into the first state, and a death from every state of people | `ss.birth(S, ...)`, `ss.death(I, ...)` |
| The sim's own results | `alive`, `died`, and `emigrated` (and, as agents, `female`) | `record_people=False` on the sim |
| A result of code named `new_...`, `n_...`, `cum_...`, or `...prevalence` | A flow, a stock, a stock, and a ratio; with none of these and no `kind=`, a flow if an integer, else a ratio, with a warning | `kind=` |
| Each `ss.BoolState` of a module written as code, and each alias given as a function | A result of the same name, the number for whom it is true | `ss.BoolArr`, for no result |
| `ss.AgentDisease` | The states `susceptible` and `infected` (with `infectious` an alias of `infected`), and the results `prevalence` and `infection`; a test detects `infected`, and a treatment calls `clear_infection()` | A state `infectious` of its own, as `ssl.AgentSEIR` has |
